title: Chapter 7 Quiz: Generative AI & LLMs
description: Assess comprehension of generative models, LLM pretraining, alignment (RLHF/DPO), prompt engineering, and RAG architectures.

questions.question: What is the mathematical distinction between a Discriminative model and a Generative model?
options: Discriminative models model P(Y|X); Generative models model P(X, Y) or P(X)
Discriminative models use GPUs; Generative models do not
Generative models can only output numbers
Discriminative models cannot be trained with gradient descent
questions.explanation: Discriminative models estimate decision boundaries P(Y|X), whereas Generative models estimate data distributions P(X, Y) to synthesize new samples.

questions.question: How do modern Diffusion Models generate high-resolution images from text prompts?
options: By gradually denoising pure Gaussian noise step-by-step conditioned on text embeddings
By solving linear systems of equations
questions.explanation: Diffusion models learn the reverse process of slowly removing noise from an image, synthesizing crisp visuals from static.

questions.question: What is the pretraining objective of causal Large Language Models (like GPT)?
options: Predicting the next token given preceding context
Classifying sentences as true or false
questions.explanation: Autoregressive LLMs are trained to maximize the log-probability of predicting the next token in continuous sequence.

questions.question: A raw 'Base Model' fresh out of pretraining is already an aligned, polite conversational assistant.
questions.explanation: False. Base models are probabilistic text completers; they require post-training instruction tuning and alignment to act as assistants.

questions.question: What does RLHF stand for in AI model alignment pipelines?
questions.explanation: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) steers model behavior to align with human preferences.

questions.question: How does Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) improve upon traditional RLHF?
options: It removes the need for training data
It implicitly optimizes the policy directly on preference pairs without training a separate reward model or using PPO
questions.explanation: DPO derives a closed-form loss directly over preference data, bypassing unstable PPO reinforcement learning and separate reward models.

questions.question: What is LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) in LLM fine-tuning?
options: A PEFT method that freezes base model weights and injects trainable low-rank decomposition rank matrices
A method for deleting bad tokens
questions.explanation: LoRA decomposes weight updates into low-rank matrices delta_W = A * B, drastically slashing memory requirements while matching full fine-tuning.

questions.question: In Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, instructing an LLM to 'think step-by-step' triggers the generation of intermediate reasoning tokens.
questions.explanation: True. Intermediate reasoning tokens allow the model to dedicate compute steps to decomposing complex multi-step problems.

questions.question: What does RAG stand for in enterprise AI architecture?
questions.explanation: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) fetches relevant external documents to ground the LLM's generative response.

questions.question: Why is RAG preferred over full model retraining when updating an AI with rapidly changing corporate knowledge?
options: RAG requires retraining all 70B weights daily
RAG is fast, cost-effective, avoids model hallucinations, and provides traceable source citations
RAG deletes the model's neural network
RAG works without any internet connection
questions.explanation: RAG dynamically queries external databases, providing up-to-date knowledge without expensive, time-consuming retraining cycles.

questions.question: In a RAG system, what type of database is used to store document chunk vectors and perform fast semantic similarity searches?
questions.explanation: Vector databases specialize in high-dimensional indexing and Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search.

questions.question: A model 'hallucination' occurs when an LLM generates factually false or unverifiable statements with high confidence.
questions.explanation: True. Hallucinations stem from statistical fluency divorced from ground-truth verification.

questions.question: What parameter controls the randomness of token generation during LLM decoding?
questions.explanation: Temperature scales the logits before Softmax: lower values (e.g. 0.0) produce deterministic outputs, while higher values increase randomness.

questions.question: What is 'Top-p' (Nucleus) sampling in generative decoding?
options: Selecting only the top 1 most probable token
Sampling only from the smallest set of top tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds threshold p
Sampling randomly across all 50,000 vocabulary tokens
questions.explanation: Nucleus sampling cuts off the unreliable long tail of low-probability tokens dynamically based on cumulative mass p.

questions.question: Providing a few input-output demonstrations directly inside the prompt is called ______-shot prompting.
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting conditions the model in-context with sample demonstrations without gradient updates.

questions.question: Chunking documents into overlapping segments (e.g., 500 tokens with 50-token overlap) prevents losing contextual meaning at chunk boundaries.
questions.explanation: True. Overlapping boundaries preserve semantic flow across fragmented document splits in RAG pipelines.

questions.question: What is Quantization (e.g., 4-bit or 8-bit quantization) in LLM deployment?
options: Reducing the numerical precision of weights from FP16 to INT8 or INT4 to slash RAM and run on smaller hardware
questions.explanation: Quantization reduces weight precision (e.g. FP16 to 4-bit AWQ/GGUF), cutting memory usage by 75% with minimal accuracy loss.

questions.question: What role does a 'System Prompt' play in conversational LLM interactions?
options: It establishes the overarching persona, behavioral constraints, safety guidelines, and operational scope for the model
It resets the GPU clock rate
questions.explanation: System prompts set the foundational behavior, instructions, tone, and guardrails for the dialogue session.

questions.question: Scaling Laws demonstrate that model loss decreases predictably as a power-law function of compute, dataset size, and parameter count.
questions.explanation: True. Empirical scaling laws (Kaplan et al., Hoffmann et al.) establish predictable power-law performance gains with scale.

questions.question: What is Re-ranking in an advanced RAG pipeline?
options: Using a cross-encoder model to re-score and rank candidate retrieved chunks for precise relevance before sending to the LLM
questions.explanation: Re-rankers examine query and candidate documents simultaneously to filter out false-positive vector matches.
